Apple___Apple_scab.description: Apple scab is a fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis. It is one of the most common and serious diseases of apple trees worldwide, causing significant economic losses.
symptoms: Olive-green or brown spots on leaves
Velvety or scabby lesions on fruit
causes: Infected leaf litter from previous season
prevention: Apply fungicide sprays from bud break
treatment: Use myclobutanil or tebuconazole for systemic control
fertilizers: Calcium-rich fertilizers to strengthen cell walls
Avoid excess nitrogen which promotes succulent growth

Apple___Black_rot.description: Black rot of apple is caused by the fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa. It affects leaves, fruit, and bark.
symptoms: Circular brown spots with purple margins on leaves
prevention: Prune out dead or diseased wood
fertilizers: Potassium fertilizers to improve fruit quality

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: Cedar apple rust is caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae. It requires both apple and eastern red cedar hosts to complete its life cycle.
symptoms: Yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface
Orange tube-like structures on leaf undersides
causes: Presence of both apple and juniper trees
fertilizers: Micronutrient supplements with zinc and manganese

Apple___healthy.description: The apple plant appears healthy with no signs of disease. Continue good agricultural practices.

Blueberry___healthy.description: Blueberry plant is healthy and shows no disease symptoms.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew on cherry is caused by Podosphaera clandestina, appearing as white powdery growth on young leaves and shoots.
symptoms: Curling and distortion of young leaves

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: Cherry plant is healthy with no disease symptoms.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.disease_name: Gray Leaf Spot / Cercospora Leaf Spot
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: Gray leaf spot (GLS) caused by Cercospora zeae-maydis is one of the most significant yield-limiting diseases of corn worldwide.
symptoms: Premature leaf death in severe cases
causes: High humidity and extended leaf wetness
fertilizers: Balanced NPK especially nitrogen for vigorous growth

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Common rust of corn caused by Puccinia sorghi. Severe infections can reduce yield by reducing photosynthesis.
symptoms: Small circular to elongated reddish-brown pustules on leaves
Shredding of leaf tissue in severe cases
prevention: Early planting to avoid peak rust season

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: Northern leaf blight (NLB) caused by Exserohilum turcicum can cause significant yield losses, especially when it infects plants early.
symptoms: Tan centers with dark green to gray borders
Lesions produce dark spores in humid conditions
Blighting of entire leaves in severe cases
causes: High humidity and prolonged leaf wetness
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids with Ht genes
treatment: Repeat applications if disease pressure is high

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: Corn plant is healthy and growing normally. Continue current agronomic practices.
fertilizers: Urea or ammonium nitrate for nitrogen

Grape___Black_rot.description: Grape black rot caused by Guignardia bidwellii can destroy up to 80% of the fruit crop in wet seasons.
symptoms: Brown circular lesions with black borders on leaves
Tan lesions on shoots and tendrils
causes: Infected mummified berries from previous season
prevention: Remove mummified berries and infected canes
treatment: Apply every 10-14 days during wet periods

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: Esca is a complex grapevine trunk disease caused by multiple fungal pathogens. It is a serious, chronic disease with no cure.
fertilizers: Balanced nutrition to maintain vine vigor

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: Isariopsis leaf spot is caused by Pseudocercospora vitis. It causes premature defoliation and may impact fruit quality.
symptoms: Irregular dark brown to black spots on leaves
prevention: Improve air circulation through canopy management

Grape___healthy.description: Grape vine is healthy with no signs of disease.
prevention: Regular scouting for pests and disease
fertilizers: Potassium in summer for fruit quality

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: Huanglongbing (HLB), also called citrus greening, is the most devastating citrus disease worldwide. Caused by Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, it has no cure.
causes: Spread by Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri)
prevention: Control Asian citrus psyllid with insecticides
Remove and destroy infected trees promptly
treatment: Nutritional treatments to extend productive life
fertilizers: Micronutrient foliar sprays to support symptomatic trees
Balanced citrus fertilizer to maintain vigor

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot of peach caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni affects leaves, fruit, and twigs.
symptoms: Water-soaked spots on leaves turning angular and brown
Shot-hole appearance as lesions drop out
treatment: Copper hydroxide or copper sulfate sprays
Apply during dormancy and early season
fertilizers: Adequate calcium to strengthen cell walls

Peach___healthy.description: Peach tree is healthy with no disease symptoms.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot of pepper caused by Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria is a major disease in warm wet growing regions.
symptoms: Brown angular spots with yellow halo

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: Bell pepper plant is healthy and showing normal growth.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Potato early blight is caused by Alternaria solani. It typically affects older leaves first and can cause significant defoliation and yield loss.
symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric rings (target pattern)
Spots appear first on older lower leaves
causes: Wet conditions alternating with dry periods
prevention: Rotate crops away from solanaceous plants for 3 years
treatment: Apply every 7-10 days during wet conditions

Potato___Late_blight.description: Potato late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans is the most devastating disease of potato, historically responsible for the Irish Famine. It can destroy an entire crop within days.
symptoms: Water-soaked pale green to brown lesions on leaves
White sporulation on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Dark brown to black stem lesions
Rotten firm brown lesions on tubers
causes: Rain and fog for extended periods
prevention: Apply preventive fungicides before disease appears
treatment: Apply preventively every 5-7 days during high-risk periods

Potato___healthy.description: Potato plant is healthy with vigorous growth and no signs of disease.

Raspberry___healthy.description: Raspberry cane is healthy with no disease symptoms.
prevention: Remove old fruiting canes after harvest

Soybean___healthy.description: Soybean plant is healthy with vigorous growth.
fertilizers: Inoculant with Bradyrhizobium for nitrogen fixation

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: Powdery mildew on squash caused by Podosphaera xanthii is very common in squash and other cucurbits.
symptoms: White powdery spots on upper leaf surface
causes: Dry warm days with cool nights

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: Strawberry leaf scorch caused by Diplocarpon earlianum appears as small dark spots that merge and cause leaf edges to appear scorched.
symptoms: Small dark purple spots on leaves
causes: Wet conditions in spring and fall

Strawberry___healthy.description: Strawberry plant is healthy with no visible disease.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Tomato bacterial spot caused by Xanthomonas vesicatoria is a major disease in warm wet climates affecting leaves, stems, and fruit.
symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots turning brown

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Tomato early blight caused by Alternaria solani typically starts on older leaves and moves upward, causing significant defoliation and reduced yields.
symptoms: Dark brown spots with distinctive concentric rings (bull's-eye pattern)
Dark sunken cankers at stem base
prevention: Stake plants to keep foliage off soil
Apply mulch to prevent soil splash
treatment: Azoxystrobin or propiconazole for systemic control
Apply every 7-10 days during wet season

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Tomato late blight caused by Phytophthora infestans is the most destructive tomato disease. Under favorable conditions it can destroy an entire field within days.
symptoms: White downy growth on underside of leaves
Greasy firm brown lesions on fruit
prevention: Apply preventive fungicides before disease appears
treatment: Apply every 5-7 days when conditions favor disease
fertilizers: Potassium and calcium to strengthen cell walls

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: Tomato leaf mold caused by Passalora fulva is primarily a problem in greenhouse tomatoes but also occurs in field crops.
symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to grayish-purple velvety mold on lower leaf surface
Affected leaves turn brown and drop

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria leaf spot caused by Septoria lycopersici is one of the most common and destructive tomato diseases worldwide.
symptoms: Small circular spots 3-6mm with dark borders and tan/white centers
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) in center of spots

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Two-spotted spider mite (Tetranychus urticae) is a major pest of tomatoes causing stippling, bronzing, and leaf drop through feeding damage.
symptoms: Fine stippling or bronzing on leaf surface
Bronze or silver sheen on leaves
causes: Hot dry conditions favor rapid reproduction
treatment: Predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) for biological control
fertilizers: Adequate nitrogen to maintain plant vigor

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: Target spot of tomato caused by Corynespora cassiicola affects leaves, stems, and fruit, often causing significant defoliation.
symptoms: Circular spots with concentric rings (target pattern) on leaves
Dark brown lesions with yellow halo

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) is a begomovirus transmitted by the silverleaf whitefly. It is one of the most damaging tomato viruses globally.
symptoms: Upward curling and yellowing of leaf margins
causes: TYLCV begomovirus transmitted by Bemisia tabaci whitefly
treatment: No cure – infected plants must be removed
Control whitefly vector with imidacloprid or thiamethoxam
Mineral oil sprays to repel whitefly
fertilizers: Maintain plant nutrition to support partially tolerant varieties

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Tomato mosaic virus (ToMV) is a tobamovirus that can cause significant yield loss. It is highly persistent in soil and on surfaces.
symptoms: Mosaic pattern of light and dark green on leaves
causes: Transmission by contact – infected hands, tools, clothing
Extremely stable – persists years in soil
prevention: Disinfect tools with 20% skim milk or 10% bleach
treatment: Heat treatment of seed (70°C for 2 days)
fertilizers: Maintain balanced nutrition to support immune plant growth

Tomato___healthy.description: Tomato plant is healthy, vigorous, and showing no disease symptoms. Keep up your excellent crop management!
fertilizers: NPK 8-32-16 at planting for root development
Calcium nitrate every 2 weeks during fruiting
Magnesium sulfate if deficiency symptoms appear
